entry_base_features: day usage;number vmail messages
hypothesis: 10110 = relu(0.89*dayCharge - 0.95*vmailMessages - 0.801), readout +1.39: high day charge raises churn, but only for customers without voicemail messages. With 0 messages the hinge starts at about 0.29 SD of day charge (about $33.3, 196 minutes); each 13.5 messages pushes the threshold up by about 1 SD, so it is on for 38% of no-voicemail customers and 1% of the others. Mean contribution +1.30 logit at 250-300 day minutes, +2.36 above 300. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00106); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.896 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.545; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.903.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: Heavy-usage detector with a service-call bump that heavy usage switches off. 7701 = relu(1.23*dayCharge + 1.46*eveMinutes - 0.506); 5611 = relu(0.60*dayCharge + 0.69*7701 + 0.01*state:40 - 0.763) = relu(1.45*dayCharge + 1.01*eveMinutes - 1.11) when 7701 is on; readout +1.30. So churn rises steeply (about 1.9 logit per SD of day charge) once combined day+evening usage is high: 5611 is on for 27% of rows (churn 27% vs 9%); mean contribution +1.69 logit at 250-300 day minutes and +3.48 above 300. 10992 = relu(0.68*custServCalls - 1.48*5611 - 0.585), readout +1.22: extra churn from customer-service calls (on for 73-100% of rows with 3+ calls; +0.63 logit at 4 calls, +1.9 at 6), cancelled when 5611 is large (heavy users who call are not penalised again). The state:40 weight (0.01) is negligible. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.0121); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.878 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.863; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.896.

family_name: service calls x low day usage
entry_base_features: day usage;intl usage;number customer service calls;state;total day calls
hypothesis: 104 = relu(-0.71*dayMinutes + 0.54*custServCalls - 0.27*state:22 + 0.09*2546 - 0.489), readout +1.54: many customer-service calls AND low day usage -> churn (train: customers with 4+ calls and under 160 day minutes churn 88%, vs 26% at 160-250 minutes). Mean contribution +0.03 logit at 0 calls, +0.89 at 4, +2.6 at 6+. state:22 subtracts 0.27*7 = 1.9 from the pre-activation, so the unit is almost never on in state 22 (1.3% vs 29% of rows): a state-specific exception fitted to 80 rows. 2546 = relu(0.20*custServCalls + 0.28*4382 - 0.915) and 4382 = relu(0.28*dayCalls - 0.17*intlCharge - 0.48) are a nearly dead side chain (2546 on for 0.1% of rows, weight 0.09). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00254); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.893 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.595; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.904.

entry_base_features: day usage;voice mail plan
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: two ReLU hinges on daytime usage that raise churn for heavy day users, mainly those without a voice-mail plan. total_day_minutes and total_day_charge are identical after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so the leaf uses both interchangeably. 1254 = relu(0.42*day - 0.73): on for day z > 1.74 (164 rows, churn 62% vs 12%), logit +2.08 per unit (up to +1.26). 3460 = relu(0.86*day - 0.83*voice_mail_plan - 0.85): on for day z > 0.39 without a voice-mail plan, z > 2.5 with one (995 rows, churn 28% vs 9.5%), logit +2.25 per unit (up to +5.3). EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form above (max err 0.002); sensitivity: 3460 driven by voice_mail_plan (0.21) and day (0.21 total). Combined usage logit (with totalChargeChain): no voice-mail plan, day z>1 and eve z>1 -> +5.2 logit, empirical churn 94%; same usage with a voice-mail plan -> churn 10%. Replacing this leaf by its best linear fit costs 0.008 train AUC; mean-ablating 3460 costs 0.016.

entry_base_features: day usage;international plan;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: customer-service-call hinges, with an interaction against day usage: many calls by low-usage customers = churn. 9203 = relu(0.66*cs - 0.67) is on at >=3 calls (848 rows, churn 25%), logit +1.41 per unit. 5395 = relu(0.71*cs - 0.65*day_charge - 0.75) is on at >=4 calls unless day z > ~0.9, or 3 calls with below-average day usage (810 rows), logit +1.93 per unit (up to +6.0). 553 = relu(0.51*cs + 0.28*international_plan - 0.68*state:41 - 0.66): >=1 call with an international plan or >=4 without (555 rows, churn 46%); reaches the logit only via the always-on relay (+0.14 per unit, max +0.45); state:41 rows switch it off (66 rows, effect <= 0.15 logit). EVIDENCE (train): table of this leaf's logit contribution / empirical churn by calls x day z-bin: 4 calls & day z<-1: +3.8 / 95%; 4 calls & day z>1: +0.8 / 33%; 5 calls & day z<-1: +5.6 / 100%; <=2 calls: ~0 / 5-9% (except the high-usage bin, handled by the usage leaves). number_customer_service_calls has no direct edge to the output, so this leaf is its only route: mean-ablating the leaf costs 0.113 train AUC; replacing it by its best linear fit costs 0.021, the largest nonlinear gain of any part.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;intl usage;number vmail messages;state
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a hinge chain on the combined day+evening bill. 5604 = relu(1.14*day_charge + 1.26*eve_charge - 0.94) (eve_charge == eve_minutes after z-scoring) is on for 1143 rows (churn 26%); 4045 = relu(0.60*day_charge + 0.73*5604 - 1.02) sharpens it (626 rows, churn 41% vs 9%), logit +1.57 per unit (up to +7.0). 9871 = relu(0.49*5604 - 0.84) is a higher threshold (244 rows, churn 56%) with a small negative logit weight (-0.24) and a tiny relay path. 387 = relu(0.94 - 1.07*vmail_messages + 0.56*intl_minutes + 0.04*state:1 - 0.86*4045) is on for 76% of rows; its -0.36 output weight lowers churn for customers with few voice-mail messages and many international minutes, and a high bill switches it off (removing that negative term). EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.008), sensitivity (4045: eve 0.14, day 0.22; 387: vmail messages 0.81, intl minutes 0.42). Linearising the leaf costs 0.008 AUC; jointly with dayUsageHinges 0.025 (the two overlap: both are day-usage hinges).

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;intl usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: Hypothesis: a low-usage hinge whose threshold rises with customer service calls (CSC). 807 = relu(-1.36 dayMin + 0.05 CSC + 0.69*2627 + 0.61*2796 - 1.30), where 2627 = 1.01 + 0.32 relu(0.87 CSC - 0.09) (always positive, affine in a CSC hinge) and 2796 = relu(0.41 - 1.00 eveCharge + 0.37 CSC + 0.15 state:41 + 0.34*12926), with 12926/13061 a two-stage CSC hinge that turns on at 3 calls. 1264 = relu(0.077 - 0.32 intlCharge + 0.39*807) adds 0.39*807 and a convex low-intl-charge hinge. Readout 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 (252 is near dead, readout -2e-5, and holds a state:2/state:44/state:4 path). Evidence (train, n=4000): sensitivity of 807 is dayMin 0.63, eveCharge 0.22, CSC 0.20. Mean gate logit rises 1.1 -> 7.4 from 0 to 7 calls. With the backbone +2.02 dayMin, the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; for CSC>=4 the low-usage arm dominates (empirical churn 0.88 low-day vs 0.24 high-day, which the network reproduces). The same hinge also lifts low-CSC, very-low-day customers (93 rows, predicted 0.17 vs empirical 0.04): a mild overextension. totalEveCharge equals totalEveMinutes after z-scoring, so the gate effectively uses evening usage. Ablation: linearising this gate drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone on the fully linearised model gives 0.836 -> 0.899. It is the source of nearly all of the network s gain over a linear model.

entry_base_features: number customer service calls;total eve calls
hypothesis: Customer-service-calls threshold. 1044 = relu(0.722 csc - 0.006 eveCalls - 0.718), output weight +1.65. csc z-levels: 0..9 calls = -1.20 + 0.766k, so the unit is 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.12 logit at 3 calls, +1.03 at 4, then +0.92 per extra call (eveCalls term negligible). Combined with the direct +0.37 logit/call slope this makes the CS-call effect convex: observed churn rate 0.11 for 0-3 calls, 0.44 at 4, 0.57 at 5, 0.68 at 6. Evidence: closed form max err 0.001; heatmap(train, 4000 rows) shows dependence on csc only. Linearising this unit alone costs 0.0067 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model adds +0.022.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;number customer service calls
hypothesis: 3151 = relu(0.515 day + 0.508 relu(0.921 day - 0.075) + 0.585 relu(0.93 day + 1.18 eveCharge + 0.189) - 0.384 csc - 0.957), output weight +1.73. A convex function of day minutes and evening charge (eveCharge == eveMinutes after z-scoring; the network uses only the charge column), switched down by CS calls. Mean logit added by day-minutes bin (q0-20,20-40,40-60,60-80,80-90,90-100) x eve tercile: 0 below the median; 0.03/0.24/1.29 in 60-80%; 0.40/1.19/2.34 in 80-90%; 1.96/3.02/4.43 in the top decile, matching churn rates up to 0.71 for top-day x top-eve. With >=4 CS calls the term is much smaller (e.g. 0.32 vs 1.34 in the 80-90% bin), so high-usage and many-calls risks do not stack. Evidence: closed form err 0.009; sensitivity (train) spread over day copies (0.17,0.16,0.14), eveCharge 0.21, csc 0.12. This is the single largest nonlinear source: linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.899 -> 0.874; restoring it alone onto the linearised model raises 0.840 -> 0.889.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage
hypothesis:
High-usage hinge: 3227 = relu(-1.044 + 0.972*dayMinutes + 0.363*eveMinutes + 0.371*relu(0.177+0.382*eveMinutes)), read out with weight 3.019. Zero for typical usage, rising steeply for the heaviest day (and evening) users, the well-known high-bill churn segment.

Evidence (train, n=4000): High-usage hinge 3.019*relu(-1.044 + 0.972*dayMin + 0.363*eveMin + 0.371*relu(0.177+0.382*eveMin)). Zero for the lower 50% of day minutes; active in 13% of the 6th-7th deciles, 48% of the 9th and 93% of the top decile, where its mean logit term is +2.32 and train churn is 0.49 (vs 0.06-0.17 elsewhere). The inner eve-minutes relu makes the eve slope 0.363 (low eve) or 0.505 (high eve): heavy day+eve users (high total bill) churn. Linear R2 of the term only 0.41. Train AUC: mean-ablation -> 0.860; linearised -> 0.873.

family_name: service calls x low day usage
entry_base_features: day usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): customer-service-calls x low-day-usage interaction. 104 = relu(0.576 + 0.755 CSC + 1.309 relu(0.332 CSC - 0.212) - 0.862 dayCharge - 1.939 relu(1.429 dayCharge + 1.216) + 0.206 state30 + 0.006 state6 + 1.688 h2039), read out 0.617*h104 + 0.688*relu(0.980 h104 - 0.618). Logit grows ~0.7-1.4 per service call and falls with day charge (slope -3.6 per z while 4834 is on), reaching zero above the day-charge median. Evidence (train, 4000 rows): mean contribution 1.13 (0 calls) to 6.97 (6 calls) in the lowest day-charge decile, 0 above p50 for <=4 calls; active on 32% of rows; sensitivity dominated by dayCharge (0.64) and CSC (0.29). For low-call, low-usage customers it cancels the negative part of the linear dayMinutes slope (+1.105 per z), so day usage below p75 has an almost flat net effect. Side inputs: state30 shifts 104 (row effect -0.85..+1.13, mean -0.15 net of its direct edge); 2039 (state9-gated) is active on only 3 train rows (CSC 8-9). Linearising this child alone costs 0.012 train AUC; restoring it alone to the all-linear model gains 0.050.

entry_base_features: day usage;number customer service calls
hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): a second service-calls threshold gated off by high day charge. 7506 = relu(-0.687 + 0.739 CSC - 2.266 relu(0.859 dayCharge - 0.133)), read out 1.195*h7506 + 1.451*relu(0.242 + 0.773 h7506) (9029 always on: constant 0.35 plus net slope 2.32 on h7506). Evidence (train): +0.35 constant for 0-2 calls; from 3 calls it adds ~+1.3 logit per extra call when day charge is below its median, much less in p50-75 and nothing above p75 (except 7+ calls). Active on 12.8% of rows. Together with csc_low_day_gate the model matches the empirical pattern: CSC>=4 & day charge <p25 churn 0.90-1.00 (model 0.81-0.84); CSC>=4 & day charge >p50 churn 0.19-0.20 (model 0.20-0.25); CSC 0-3 churn 0.04-0.06 below p75 (model 0.05-0.07). The two gates are largely redundant: linearising either alone costs only 0.012-0.013 AUC, both together 0.063.

entry_base_features: day usage;state
hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): high-usage hinge. 6238 = relu(-0.508 + 0.769 dayMinutes - 0.018 state34), read out 1.725. Zero for the bottom ~75% of day minutes (z<0.66), +0.36 logit at p75-90 and +1.46 above p90, where churn is 0.49 vs 0.06-0.15 below. Adds to the linear +1.105 day-minutes slope (dayMinutes == dayCharge after z-scoring, so this and the dayCharge gates read the same quantity). state34's weight is negligible (row effect <=0.21). Restoring it alone to the all-linear model gains 0.023 train AUC; linearising it alone costs 0.002.

family_name: heavy day usage without voice mail
entry_base_features: day usage;number customer service calls;number vmail messages
hypothesis: 2899 = relu(0.72*dayCharge - 0.88*vmailMessages - 0.25*CSC - 0.55), readout +3.00: high day charge raises churn, but only for customers with no voicemail messages, and a little less for customers who call service (these are covered by the service-call units). For no-voicemail customers the mean contribution is +0.44 logit at 180-200 day minutes, +1.95 at 220-250, +3.41 at 250-300 and +5.44 above 300 (train churn 21%, 55%, 95%); for voicemail users it is about 0 below 300 minutes. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form and local table attached. Largest single nonlinear source: linearised (R2 0.58) AUC 0.910 -> 0.897; mean-ablated -> 0.848; restored alone onto the linearised model 0.834 -> 0.888. Largely redundant with heavy_day_eve_usage (both are high-day-usage hinges).

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;state
hypothesis: 1694 = relu(1.09*dayMinutes + 0.78*eveCharge + 0.02*state:20 - 0.04*state:27 - 0.85), readout +1.60: a hinge on combined day+evening usage. Zero unless day and evening usage are both well above average; mean contribution +0.55 at 200-250 day and 200-250 evening minutes, +2.05 at 250-300/200-250, +4.7 when both are above 250/300 (train churn 63-83% in those cells). The state:20 (+0.37 at most) and state:27 (-0.43 at most) weights are small per-state shifts of the threshold. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form and day x evening table attached. Linearised (R2 0.50) AUC 0.910 -> 0.902; restored alone onto the linearised model 0.834 -> 0.872. Overlaps with day_charge_no_voicemail.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: Many customer-service calls AND low day usage -> churn. 7689 = relu(0.85*CSC + 0.30); 15054 = relu(1.11*dayCharge + 1.09*state:43 + 1.09); 4397 = relu(0.78*15054 - 0.74*state:0 - 0.81*state:35 - 0.52) is a day-charge ramp; 997 = relu(0.20*CSC + 0.23*7689 - 0.49*4397 - 0.41) fires when service calls are high and day charge low. 9974 = 1.05*997 + 0.066 is always on, so the output sees about 4.81*997: 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.45 logit at 3 calls with under 160 day minutes, +1.9 at 4 calls, +3.5 at 5 and +5 at 6+ (train churn for 4+ calls and under 160 minutes is 80-100%, vs 7-34% above 200 minutes). Rare-state switches inside the gate: state:43 (95 rows) adds +9.4 to 15054 and switches the rule off entirely (up to -2.4 logit on affected rows); state:0 and state:35 subtract about 6-7 from 4397 and switch the day-usage brake off, so in those states service calls alone trigger it (up to +2.0 logit). 5728 = relu(0.99*state:6 + 0.11*997 + 0.64) is always on; 827 = relu(1.06*state:12 + 0.30*eveCharge - 1.60*5728 - 0.75) is on only in state:12 (55 rows) and with readout -0.018 gives about -0.13 logit there; state:6 has no net effect. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form attached; local table of mean contribution by calls x day-minutes bin attached. Linearising this child (least squares on its 8 entry inputs, R2 0.39) lowers train AUC 0.910 -> 0.899; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model raises AUC 0.834 -> 0.872.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;night usage;state;voice mail plan
hypothesis:
Total-usage score. 1406=relu(0.537*dayCharge-0.882*state41-0.508); 7558=relu(0.511+0.660*eveMinutes+1.204*1406); 879=relu(-0.996+0.548*7558+0.521*dayMinutes+0.213*nightMinutes-1.011*voiceMailPlan). A hinge on a weighted sum of day (charge and minutes, identical after z-scoring), evening and night usage, lowered by having a voicemail plan; zero for ~2/3 of customers (light/average users).

Evidence (train, n=4000): 879 is a single hinge on a usage score. Pre-activation = -0.996 + 0.521*dayMinutes + 0.213*nightMinutes - 1.011*voiceMailPlan + 0.548*relu(0.511 + 0.660*eveMinutes + 1.204*relu(-0.508 + 0.537*dayCharge - 0.882*state41)). dayCharge and dayMinutes are the same column after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so day usage enters twice (directly and via 1406); eve and night likewise equal their charge columns. 879 is active in 34% of train rows: 1% of the lowest day-minute decile, 78% of the top decile. Voicemail-plan customers (1,061 rows): 879 is NEVER active (0/1061), so the whole usage risk is switched off for them; it is active in 46% of non-voicemail rows. State 41 (66 rows) forces 1406 off (0/66), removing the day-charge feed for those rows. Linear R2 of 879 on its inputs: 0.53. Sensitivity (train, n=4000): voiceMailPlan 0.34, dayMinutes 0.18, eveMinutes 0.11, state41 0.08, nightMinutes 0.07, dayCharge 0.05.

entry_base_features: day usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: 776 = relu(-0.567 + 1.565*relu(0.603*CSC-0.325) - 0.086*relu(0.993*CSC-0.196) - 0.782*day - 0.138*state22 - 0.589*state29) (day = dayCharge = dayMinutes after z-scoring; -0.836*dayCharge + 0.054*dayMinutes), read out with +1.646 on the logit. It is a customer-service-calls x low-day-usage interaction. The CSC term turns on from 3 calls (6258) and grows linearly; the unit is on when day usage is below a threshold that rises with CSC: day z < -0.6 for 0-2 calls (a weak low-usage hinge), < 0.0 at 3 calls, < 0.8 at 4, < 1.6 at 5+. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): on for 26% of rows with 0-2 calls but 78-100% with 4+ calls; mean logit contribution 0.2 (0-2 calls) -> 1.07 (4 calls) -> 3.6 (6 calls); among 4+ callers with low day usage (z<-0.5) churn is 0.87-1.0 and the unit adds +2.5 to +4.9. Linear fit R2 0.54; linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.905 -> 0.894; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gains +0.050 AUC. Sensitivity: dayCharge 0.28, state29 0.20, CSC 0.11. state29 (72 rows) switches the unit off entirely (z=7.4 gives -4.35 pre-activation): for the 28 state-29 rows where it would be on, it removes 0.95 logit on average (1 churner among them). state22 removes up to 0.86. These are rare-category switches. For 0-2 callers with very low day usage (z<-2, 93 rows) the unit and 4496 overshoot the direct day slope, giving a logit 0.7 above the empirical log-odds (mild U-shape artefact).

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;number customer service calls
hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: 4496 = relu(-1.966 - 1.843*dayMinutes - 0.859*eveCharge + g(CSC)), read out with +0.809. g is a monotone piecewise-linear function of CSC from the chain 7068 = relu(0.577*CSC-0.148) (on from 2 calls) -> 7561, 11555, 12924, 9009 (always on, so affine in 7068) plus 10362 = relu(0.933*7068-0.505) (on from 4 calls, an extra kink); g = 2.23 at 0-1 calls, 2.30 at 2, then about +0.8 per extra call (3.04 at 3, 3.88 at 4, 5.58 at 6). So 4496 is a below-average day+evening usage hinge (0.26 - 1.84*day - 0.86*eve > 0 at 0-1 calls) whose threshold and height rise with service calls. EVIDENCE (train): on for 52% of 0-call rows, 82% at 4 calls, 100% at 7+; mean logit contribution 0.74 at 0 calls, 1.56 at 4, 3.65 at 6. With the +1.92 direct dayCharge edge it makes the day effect convex: slope 1.92 above average usage, 0.43 below (and about -0.86 below z=-0.73 together with 776). Linear fit R2 0.78; linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.905 -> 0.889; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gains +0.056. Sensitivity: dayMinutes 1.09, eveCharge 0.51, CSC 0.29. eveCharge equals eveMinutes after z-scoring (the backbone also uses both).

entry_base_features: eve usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis:
Customer-service-calls threshold. 11061 = relu(0.811 CSC - 0.648) read out with weight 2.11 switches on from 3 calls. The rest of the cluster (9657 -> 651 -> 886 -> 6256/14188, 10375 -> 7530) is dead or constant on train; 14188 acts as a state:47 one-hot switch because 886 is always 0.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Local table (train) by number of customer service calls 0..9: churn 0.115, 0.110, 0.110, 0.106, 0.437, 0.571, 0.679, 0.545, 1.0 (1 row), 1.0 (2 rows); mean csc term 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.56, 1.87, 3.17, 4.48, 5.78, 7.41, 9.03. 11061 switches on at 3 calls (so the network fires one call early: 3-call churn is still 10.6%) then adds +1.3 logit per call. 7530 is active on 3 rows, 9657->651->886 is dead (651 max pre-activation -0.003), 6256 is the constant 0.033, 14188 = relu(0.943 state:47 - 0.005) on state:47 rows only (+0.17 logit). Linear R2 of the term 0.62. Ablation: logit-term sd 0.771, linear R2 0.616; full AUC 0.8918, replaced by its linear fit 0.8734, mean-ablated 0.8026.

entry_base_features: day usage;eve usage;number customer service calls;state
hypothesis:
Day x eve usage interaction. 103 = relu(1.39 eveCharge + 1.13) feeds a relu chain 5908 -> 10233 into 9165 = relu(0.668 dayCharge + 0.481*10233 - 0.737), read out with weight 2.17: a hinge on (day charge + increasing function of eve charge), i.e. high combined day+eve bill. 103 and 12978 read out negatively, giving a mild negative bowl in eve charge alone. 5000 (via 8513 from 9165, plus customer service calls) is a near-dead tail unit.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Local table (train): mean cascade+direct-eve logit term by (dayCharge z, eveCharge z) bin: D<0 any E: -0.25..-0.71 (churn 5-14%); D 0.5-1 & E>1.5: +1.56 (churn 44%); D 1-1.5 & E 1-1.5: +1.42 (62%); D>1.5 & E 0-0.5: +1.42 (70%); D>1.5 & E>1.5: +3.16 (77%). 9165 is on in 27.4% of rows (churn 26.8% when on vs 9.4% off). Contour is a ramp in roughly 0.668 D + 0.40 E: a combined day+eve bill threshold, which a linear model cannot represent (linear R2 of the term 0.46). 103 is 0 for eveCharge z < -0.82 (20.7% of rows). 5000 is active on only 3 train rows (8-9 customer service calls), so it is a negligible tail. totalDayCharge is identical to totalDayMinutes and totalEveCharge identical to totalEveMinutes after z-scoring. Ablation: logit-term sd 0.611, linear R2 0.459; full AUC 0.8918, replaced by its linear fit 0.8789, mean-ablated 0.8766.

excluded: input -> output edge (not graftable in C2)
